structured_output.summary: The change follows the spec steps in order. It uses this_number_value and ops::to_integer_or_infinity with `?`, so abrupt completions propagate. The non-finite check comes before the range checks, as the spec requires. -0 gives "0e+0". Step 11.a rounds on the exact decimal expansion (`{:.1100e}`, enough for any double) and rounds half up, which matches the "pick the larger" tie rule. The carry case where all digits are 9 is handled. Step 11.b uses Rust's shortest round-trip `{:e}`, which agrees with Number::toString. The two `unreachable!` lint flags guard Rust `{:e}` output that always contains an 'e' and an integer exponent, so they are acceptable. There is no special-casing, and the test262 target moved from 8 to 30 passing with no regressions.
